source: ATNF Pulsar Catalogue (Manchester et al. 2005), published values embedded in pipeline/pulsars.py
citation: Manchester, R. N., Hobbs, G. B., Teoh, A. & Hobbs, M. 2005, AJ 129, 1993

pulsars.name: Vela pulsar
pulsars.note: Born in a supernova about 11,000 years ago; glitches (spins up suddenly) every few years.

pulsars.name: Crab pulsar
pulsars.note: The remnant of the supernova Chinese astronomers saw in 1054 AD.

pulsars.name: PSR B0329+54
pulsars.note: The brightest pulsar in the northern sky.

pulsars.name: PSR J0437−4715
pulsars.note: The nearest millisecond pulsar, spun up by a white-dwarf companion; one of the steadiest clocks known.

pulsars.name: PSR B1937+21
pulsars.note: The first millisecond pulsar ever found (1982): 642 turns a second.

pulsars.name: CP 1919, the first pulsar
pulsars.note: The first pulsar ever discovered, by Jocelyn Bell Burnell in 1967.
